question: What is the main purpose of a planned flushing program in a distribution system?
correctAnswer: To remove accumulated sediment and stale water from watermains
explanation: Flushing moves water through mains at scouring velocity, carrying out sediment and replacing stale water, which protects water quality.
options: To remove accumulated sediment and stale water from watermains
To raise the treatment plant production rate
To test the accuracy of customer meters
To increase the static pressure in all zones
optionA: To remove accumulated sediment and stale water from watermains
optionB: To raise the treatment plant production rate
optionC: To test the accuracy of customer meters
optionD: To increase the static pressure in all zones
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing Program Design.

question: How does unidirectional flushing differ from simply opening a hydrant and letting water run?
correctAnswer: Valves are operated so flow is directed in one direction through a planned section of main
explanation: Unidirectional flushing uses valve operations to force flow one way through a section, building the velocity needed to scour deposits.
options: The water is discharged without any valves being touched
Valves are operated so flow is directed in one direction through a planned section of main
Only one hydrant in the whole system is ever used
The main is taken out of service and drained first
optionA: The water is discharged without any valves being touched
optionB: Valves are operated so flow is directed in one direction through a planned section of main
optionC: Only one hydrant in the whole system is ever used
optionD: The main is taken out of service and drained first
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing Program Design.

question: What is a sensible first step when designing a flushing program for a large system?
correctAnswer: Divide the system into flushing sections using pipe layout, sizes and valve locations
explanation: Planning sections around the actual pipe network and available valves lets each flush be controlled and sequenced effectively.
options: Order replacement pipe for the oldest streets
Raise the disinfectant dose at the treatment plant
Divide the system into flushing sections using pipe layout, sizes and valve locations
Close every boundary valve between pressure zones
optionA: Order replacement pipe for the oldest streets
optionB: Raise the disinfectant dose at the treatment plant
optionC: Divide the system into flushing sections using pipe layout, sizes and valve locations
optionD: Close every boundary valve between pressure zones
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing Program Design.

question: Why should flushing normally proceed from a clean water source toward areas with poorer water quality?
correctAnswer: So sediment is not drawn into sections that have already been cleaned
explanation: Working from clean to dirty protects finished sections; reversing the order can pull loosened sediment back into cleaned mains.
options: So the highest pressure zone is flushed last
So hydrants near the plant wear out first
So customers use less water during the program
So sediment is not drawn into sections that have already been cleaned
optionA: So the highest pressure zone is flushed last
optionB: So hydrants near the plant wear out first
optionC: So customers use less water during the program
optionD: So sediment is not drawn into sections that have already been cleaned
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing Program Design.

question: What flow condition is a flushing program mainly trying to achieve in the target main?
correctAnswer: A velocity high enough to scour and carry out loose sediment
explanation: Scouring depends on velocity; slow flushing moves water but leaves deposits behind in the pipe.
options: The lowest possible velocity to save water
A velocity high enough to scour and carry out loose sediment
Zero flow so sediment can settle
Flow in both directions at the same time
optionA: The lowest possible velocity to save water
optionB: A velocity high enough to scour and carry out loose sediment
optionC: Zero flow so sediment can settle
optionD: Flow in both directions at the same time
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing Program Design.

question: Which set of details should a complete watermain break record include?
correctAnswer: Location, pipe size, material, age and the type of failure observed
explanation: Consistent records of pipe attributes and failure type are what make later pattern analysis possible.
options: Only the name of the repair contractor
Only the total repair cost for the year
Location, pipe size, material, age and the type of failure observed
The water bill of the nearest customer
optionA: Only the name of the repair contractor
optionB: Only the total repair cost for the year
optionC: Location, pipe size, material, age and the type of failure observed
optionD: The water bill of the nearest customer
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Break Record Analysis.

question: Plotting several years of breaks on a system map is most useful for what?
correctAnswer: Identifying streets or segments where breaks cluster and renewal should be considered
explanation: Clusters reveal localized deterioration that a list of individual repairs can hide.
options: Setting the chlorine dose at the plant
Choosing the colour of new hydrants
Scheduling meter reading routes
Identifying streets or segments where breaks cluster and renewal should be considered
optionA: Setting the chlorine dose at the plant
optionB: Choosing the colour of new hydrants
optionC: Scheduling meter reading routes
optionD: Identifying streets or segments where breaks cluster and renewal should be considered
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Break Record Analysis.

question: A single street segment has had four breaks in three years while the rest of the system is quiet. What does this most likely suggest?
correctAnswer: Localized deterioration of that segment rather than random system wide failure
explanation: Repeated failures in one segment point to a local cause such as corrosion, soil conditions or pipe condition on that segment.
options: Localized deterioration of that segment rather than random system wide failure
That the whole system needs immediate replacement
That break records for that street should be deleted
That pressure everywhere should be doubled
optionA: Localized deterioration of that segment rather than random system wide failure
optionB: That the whole system needs immediate replacement
optionC: That break records for that street should be deleted
optionD: That pressure everywhere should be doubled
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Break Record Analysis.

question: Why do break records note soil conditions and weather at the time of failure?
correctAnswer: They help identify contributing causes such as corrosive soil or frost loading
explanation: External conditions often contribute to failure, and recording them helps separate pipe problems from environmental causes.
options: They decide the customer water rate
They replace the need to record pipe material
They help identify contributing causes such as corrosive soil or frost loading
They are required on every water bill
optionA: They decide the customer water rate
optionB: They replace the need to record pipe material
optionC: They help identify contributing causes such as corrosive soil or frost loading
optionD: They are required on every water bill
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Break Record Analysis.

question: How is a system break rate commonly expressed for year to year comparison?
correctAnswer: Breaks per 100 km of main per year
explanation: Normalizing by length of main and time lets systems and years be compared fairly regardless of system size.
options: Breaks per hydrant per shift
Breaks per customer complaint
Breaks per litre of water sold
Breaks per 100 km of main per year
optionA: Breaks per hydrant per shift
optionB: Breaks per customer complaint
optionC: Breaks per litre of water sold
optionD: Breaks per 100 km of main per year
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Break Record Analysis.

question: A standpipe shows good residual at the bottom sample tap but very low residual near the top. What is the most likely explanation?
correctAnswer: Incomplete mixing has left stratified layers of water of different ages in the tank
explanation: When stored water does not mix, older water can sit in one layer with decayed residual while fresher water stays in another layer.
options: Incomplete mixing has left stratified layers of water of different ages in the tank
The bottom sample tap is connected to a different system
The tank paint is changing the sample results
The upper water has been fully replaced daily
optionA: Incomplete mixing has left stratified layers of water of different ages in the tank
optionB: The bottom sample tap is connected to a different system
optionC: The tank paint is changing the sample results
optionD: The upper water has been fully replaced daily
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Mixing In Storage.

question: What benefit does an active tank mixer provide during a cold, low demand period?
correctAnswer: It keeps temperature and residual uniform, which also reduces ice formation
explanation: Mixing prevents thermal stratification, keeps residual even throughout the stored volume and discourages ice buildup.
options: It raises the overflow elevation of the tank
It keeps temperature and residual uniform, which also reduces ice formation
It removes the need for any tank inspection
It lets the tank be taken out of service permanently
optionA: It raises the overflow elevation of the tank
optionB: It keeps temperature and residual uniform, which also reduces ice formation
optionC: It removes the need for any tank inspection
optionD: It lets the tank be taken out of service permanently
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Mixing In Storage.

question: A tank fills and drains through one common inlet and outlet pipe. What mixing problem can this arrangement create?
correctAnswer: Short circuiting, where incoming water leaves again before mixing with the bulk of the stored water
explanation: With a single common pipe, fresh water can pass in and out near the connection while the rest of the volume stays stagnant.
options: The tank will always overflow at night
The stored water will mix too violently
The outlet water will always be the oldest water
Short circuiting, where incoming water leaves again before mixing with the bulk of the stored water
optionA: The tank will always overflow at night
optionB: The stored water will mix too violently
optionC: The outlet water will always be the oldest water
optionD: Short circuiting, where incoming water leaves again before mixing with the bulk of the stored water
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Mixing In Storage.

question: An operator suspects poor mixing in an elevated tank. Which check best confirms it?
correctAnswer: Compare residual and temperature samples taken at different depths and locations
explanation: Differences between depths show stratification directly; a single level reading says nothing about water quality inside the tank.
options: Compare residual and temperature samples taken at different depths and locations
Read the tank level gauge once at noon
Ask customers if the water tastes strong
Paint a mark at the normal operating level
optionA: Compare residual and temperature samples taken at different depths and locations
optionB: Read the tank level gauge once at noon
optionC: Ask customers if the water tastes strong
optionD: Paint a mark at the normal operating level
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Mixing In Storage.

question: A mixer is installed in a reservoir that had chronic low residuals. What is the best way to judge whether it worked?
correctAnswer: Trend residual results from several points in the reservoir and look for uniform values over time
explanation: Uniform, stable residuals across sampling points over time demonstrate that mixing has removed the stagnant zones.
options: Check that the mixer motor feels warm
Trend residual results from several points in the reservoir and look for uniform values over time
Wait for the next customer complaint
Measure only the inlet residual once
optionA: Check that the mixer motor feels warm
optionB: Trend residual results from several points in the reservoir and look for uniform values over time
optionC: Wait for the next customer complaint
optionD: Measure only the inlet residual once
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Mixing In Storage.

question: Which combination best describes the core of a residual management program?
correctAnswer: Routine monitoring at representative locations, trending of results, and set response actions when residuals fall
explanation: A program works because results are collected consistently, reviewed as trends and tied to defined operator responses.
options: One sample per year at the treatment plant only
Raising the dose whenever any customer calls
Routine monitoring at representative locations, trending of results, and set response actions when residuals fall
Recording results without ever reviewing them
optionA: One sample per year at the treatment plant only
optionB: Raising the dose whenever any customer calls
optionC: Routine monitoring at representative locations, trending of results, and set response actions when residuals fall
optionD: Recording results without ever reviewing them
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Residual Management Programs.

question: Residuals at several dead end mains are repeatedly the lowest in the system. Which program response fits best?
correctAnswer: Put those dead ends on a scheduled flushing routine
explanation: Dead ends have little natural turnover, so scheduled flushing is the standard program tool for restoring residual there.
options: Put those dead ends on a scheduled flushing routine
Raise pressure in the nearest zone
Replace all the customer meters on those streets
Sample them less often so results look better
optionA: Put those dead ends on a scheduled flushing routine
optionB: Raise pressure in the nearest zone
optionC: Replace all the customer meters on those streets
optionD: Sample them less often so results look better
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Residual Management Programs.

question: Plant effluent residual is steady, but residuals across one zone have declined steadily for three weeks. What should the operator investigate first?
correctAnswer: Water age, storage turnover and demand changes within that zone
explanation: A zone specific decline with a steady supply points to local water age, storage or demand conditions rather than treatment.
options: The colour of the zone valves
Water age, storage turnover and demand changes within that zone
The plant raw water turbidity only
Whether the sample bottles were labelled in pen
optionA: The colour of the zone valves
optionB: Water age, storage turnover and demand changes within that zone
optionC: The plant raw water turbidity only
optionD: Whether the sample bottles were labelled in pen
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Residual Management Programs.

question: What is the purpose of a booster disinfection station in a large distribution system?
correctAnswer: To raise residual in a distant part of the system without overdosing the whole system
explanation: Boosting at the point of need restores residual where it has decayed, avoiding excessive doses for customers near the plant.
options: To disinfect water before it enters treatment
To remove disinfectant from water near the plant
To raise residual in a distant part of the system without overdosing the whole system
To replace sampling in the far zone
optionA: To disinfect water before it enters treatment
optionB: To remove disinfectant from water near the plant
optionC: To raise residual in a distant part of the system without overdosing the whole system
optionD: To replace sampling in the far zone
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Residual Management Programs.

question: Why does a residual program record temperature and location along with each residual result?
correctAnswer: Residual decay varies with temperature and distance, so the context is needed to interpret trends
explanation: Warm water and long travel both speed decay; recording the context lets operators compare results fairly and spot real changes.
options: Temperature results are billed to customers
Location data is only used for payroll
It allows the lab to skip chain of custody forms
Residual decay varies with temperature and distance, so the context is needed to interpret trends
optionA: Temperature results are billed to customers
optionB: Location data is only used for payroll
optionC: It allows the lab to skip chain of custody forms
optionD: Residual decay varies with temperature and distance, so the context is needed to interpret trends
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Residual Management Programs.

question: What should a cross-connection control program inventory track for each protected premise?
correctAnswer: The hazard level, the type of backflow preventer installed and its test status
explanation: Administration depends on knowing the hazard, the device protecting against it and whether that device is tested and current.
options: The owner favourite water brand
The hazard level, the type of backflow preventer installed and its test status
Only the size of the water meter
The number of employees at the business
optionA: The owner favourite water brand
optionB: The hazard level, the type of backflow preventer installed and its test status
optionC: Only the size of the water meter
optionD: The number of employees at the business
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Cross-Connection Program Administration.

question: A testable backflow preventer at a commercial premise is well past its required test date. What is the proper program response?
correctAnswer: Notify the owner and require testing by a qualified tester, escalating under the program rules if it is not done
explanation: Devices only protect while verified; the program must follow up overdue tests through notice and enforcement steps.
options: Ignore it because the device was fine at installation
Remove the device so no test is needed
Notify the owner and require testing by a qualified tester, escalating under the program rules if it is not done
Test it by closing the customer meter for a week
optionA: Ignore it because the device was fine at installation
optionB: Remove the device so no test is needed
optionC: Notify the owner and require testing by a qualified tester, escalating under the program rules if it is not done
optionD: Test it by closing the customer meter for a week
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Cross-Connection Program Administration.

question: What does the hazard assessment of a premise determine in a cross-connection program?
correctAnswer: The degree of hazard, which sets the level of backflow protection required
explanation: Protection is matched to risk; assessing the hazard first ensures the required device fits what could actually flow back.
options: The water rate the premise will pay
The size of the service connection pipe only
Whether the premise needs a water meter
The degree of hazard, which sets the level of backflow protection required
optionA: The water rate the premise will pay
optionB: The size of the service connection pipe only
optionC: Whether the premise needs a water meter
optionD: The degree of hazard, which sets the level of backflow protection required
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Cross-Connection Program Administration.

question: A utility is prioritizing premises for cross-connection surveys. Which premises should come first?
correctAnswer: Industrial and commercial sites where chemicals or processes could contaminate the supply
explanation: Survey effort goes first where a backflow event would do the most harm, such as sites handling chemicals.
options: Industrial and commercial sites where chemicals or processes could contaminate the supply
Single family homes with no special equipment
Vacant lots with no service connection
Streetlights owned by the municipality
optionA: Industrial and commercial sites where chemicals or processes could contaminate the supply
optionB: Single family homes with no special equipment
optionC: Vacant lots with no service connection
optionD: Streetlights owned by the municipality
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Cross-Connection Program Administration.

question: Why are complete device test records important when a contamination incident is investigated?
correctAnswer: They show which premises were protected and help trace possible sources of backflow
explanation: During an incident, records let investigators confirm protection was in place and narrow the search for an unprotected source.
options: They prove the utility never needs to sample
They set the price of replacement devices
They show which premises were protected and help trace possible sources of backflow
They replace the need for a hazard assessment
optionA: They prove the utility never needs to sample
optionB: They set the price of replacement devices
optionC: They show which premises were protected and help trace possible sources of backflow
optionD: They replace the need for a hazard assessment
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Cross-Connection Program Administration.

question: Which information is combined in a watermain condition assessment?
correctAnswer: Age, material, break history, soil conditions and operating pressure
explanation: Condition is estimated from the pipe itself, its failure history and the environment it operates in.
options: The paint colour and the crew size only
Customer water use in the last month only
The day of the week each break occurred only
Age, material, break history, soil conditions and operating pressure
optionA: The paint colour and the crew size only
optionB: Customer water use in the last month only
optionC: The day of the week each break occurred only
optionD: Age, material, break history, soil conditions and operating pressure
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Asset Condition Awareness.

question: How should renewal priority be set when two mains have similar condition scores?
correctAnswer: Weigh the consequence of failure as well as the likelihood, so a critical main ranks higher
explanation: Risk combines likelihood and consequence; a failing main feeding a hospital or a trunk route deserves priority over an equal pipe serving a quiet street.
options: Weigh the consequence of failure as well as the likelihood, so a critical main ranks higher
Always replace the shorter main first
Replace whichever main a customer mentions first
Ignore consequence and use age alone
optionA: Weigh the consequence of failure as well as the likelihood, so a critical main ranks higher
optionB: Always replace the shorter main first
optionC: Replace whichever main a customer mentions first
optionD: Ignore consequence and use age alone
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Asset Condition Awareness.

question: Why are distribution valves exercised and assessed as part of an asset condition program, not just mains?
correctAnswer: A valve that will not operate during a break forces a larger shutdown and longer outage
explanation: Valves are critical control points; their condition directly affects how well the utility can respond to failures.
options: Valves are the most expensive asset to paint
A valve that will not operate during a break forces a larger shutdown and longer outage
Exercised valves increase water pressure permanently
Valve condition decides the chlorine dose
optionA: Valves are the most expensive asset to paint
optionB: A valve that will not operate during a break forces a larger shutdown and longer outage
optionC: Exercised valves increase water pressure permanently
optionD: Valve condition decides the chlorine dose
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Asset Condition Awareness.

question: What does acoustic leak detection contribute to asset condition awareness?
correctAnswer: It finds hidden leaks on mains without excavation, revealing losses and possible pipe deterioration
explanation: Listening for leak noise locates non surfacing leaks, which are both water loss and a sign of asset condition.
options: It measures the hardness of the water
It replaces the need for break records
It raises the pressure in leaking sections
It finds hidden leaks on mains without excavation, revealing losses and possible pipe deterioration
optionA: It measures the hardness of the water
optionB: It replaces the need for break records
optionC: It raises the pressure in leaking sections
optionD: It finds hidden leaks on mains without excavation, revealing losses and possible pipe deterioration
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Asset Condition Awareness.

question: A trunk main has only a moderate chance of failure but feeds a hospital and a large industrial area. How should it be treated in planning?
correctAnswer: Rank it high for inspection and renewal planning because the consequence of failure is severe
explanation: High consequence assets warrant early attention even at moderate likelihood, because an unplanned failure would be very disruptive.
options: Rank it high for inspection and renewal planning because the consequence of failure is severe
Rank it last because its failure chance is not the highest
Remove it from the asset register
Plan nothing until it actually breaks
optionA: Rank it high for inspection and renewal planning because the consequence of failure is severe
optionB: Rank it last because its failure chance is not the highest
optionC: Remove it from the asset register
optionD: Plan nothing until it actually breaks
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Asset Condition Awareness.

question: A station's energy used per cubic metre pumped has risen steadily over a year at similar flows and heads. What is the best interpretation?
correctAnswer: Pump efficiency is likely deteriorating, for example through wear, and the pump should be investigated
explanation: Rising energy per unit volume at the same duty is a classic sign of worn wear rings, impeller damage or other efficiency loss.
options: Energy use always rises and needs no attention
Pump efficiency is likely deteriorating, for example through wear, and the pump should be investigated
The water has become heavier than normal
The electricity meter must be reading customer use
optionA: Energy use always rises and needs no attention
optionB: Pump efficiency is likely deteriorating, for example through wear, and the pump should be investigated
optionC: The water has become heavier than normal
optionD: The electricity meter must be reading customer use
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy In Pumping.

question: Where storage capacity allows, why do utilities shift pumping into off peak electricity periods?
correctAnswer: Storage filled off peak can supply peak demand, cutting energy cost and demand charges
explanation: Time shifting uses the tank as an energy buffer, buying electricity when it is cheaper while service continues from storage.
options: Off peak water needs no disinfection
Pumps cannot run during the day
Storage filled off peak can supply peak demand, cutting energy cost and demand charges
Storage water evaporates less at night
optionA: Off peak water needs no disinfection
optionB: Pumps cannot run during the day
optionC: Storage filled off peak can supply peak demand, cutting energy cost and demand charges
optionD: Storage water evaporates less at night
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy In Pumping.

question: Why does controlling flow by throttling a discharge valve waste energy?
correctAnswer: The pump produces head that is then burned off as loss across the partly closed valve
explanation: Energy spent building pressure that a valve then destroys is paid for but does no useful work.
options: The pump produces head that is then burned off as loss across the partly closed valve
Throttled valves make the motor run backwards
The water becomes too clean to pump
Throttling removes air from the main
optionA: The pump produces head that is then burned off as loss across the partly closed valve
optionB: Throttled valves make the motor run backwards
optionC: The water becomes too clean to pump
optionD: Throttling removes air from the main
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy In Pumping.

question: What is the main energy advantage of a variable speed drive on a distribution pump?
correctAnswer: Speed is matched to demand, so the pump avoids the losses of running full speed and throttling
explanation: Affinity behaviour means small speed reductions cut power sharply, so matching speed to need saves substantial energy.
options: It lets the pump run without a motor
Speed is matched to demand, so the pump avoids the losses of running full speed and throttling
It removes the need for a check valve
It increases the static head of the zone
optionA: It lets the pump run without a motor
optionB: Speed is matched to demand, so the pump avoids the losses of running full speed and throttling
optionC: It removes the need for a check valve
optionD: It increases the static head of the zone
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy In Pumping.

question: Two identical pumps serve the same station. Pump A consistently uses more energy per cubic metre than Pump B at the same duty point. What is the most useful next step?
correctAnswer: Test and compare Pump A against its curve and inspect it for wear or obstruction
explanation: A side by side difference at equal duty isolates the problem to the machine, and curve testing plus inspection finds the cause.
options: Run Pump A twice as often to even things out
Raise the discharge pressure of both pumps
Test and compare Pump A against its curve and inspect it for wear or obstruction
Stop recording energy for that station
optionA: Run Pump A twice as often to even things out
optionB: Raise the discharge pressure of both pumps
optionC: Test and compare Pump A against its curve and inspect it for wear or obstruction
optionD: Stop recording energy for that station
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy In Pumping.

question: A boundary valve between a high zone and a low zone is found open. What problem can this cause?
correctAnswer: It can defeat the pressure reducing valve control, overpressuring the low zone and draining the high zone storage
explanation: An open boundary short circuits the zone separation that the pressure reducing valve is meant to maintain.
options: It will improve pressure in both zones
It only affects water billing, not pressure
It stops all flow in both zones
It can defeat the pressure reducing valve control, overpressuring the low zone and draining the high zone storage
optionA: It will improve pressure in both zones
optionB: It only affects water billing, not pressure
optionC: It stops all flow in both zones
optionD: It can defeat the pressure reducing valve control, overpressuring the low zone and draining the high zone storage
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Zone Management.

question: During peak demand, the upper zone reports low pressure while the lower zone is normal. Which checks fit the situation best?
correctAnswer: Verify pressure reducing valve operation, boundary valve positions and the upper zone storage level
explanation: Zone specific low pressure points to the equipment and storage that define that zone hydraulic grade, not to system wide sources.
options: Check only the raw water intake screens
Verify pressure reducing valve operation, boundary valve positions and the upper zone storage level
Replace customer meters in the lower zone
Flush every hydrant in the lower zone
optionA: Check only the raw water intake screens
optionB: Verify pressure reducing valve operation, boundary valve positions and the upper zone storage level
optionC: Replace customer meters in the lower zone
optionD: Flush every hydrant in the lower zone
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Zone Management.

question: Why do zone managers rely on continuous pressure logging rather than occasional spot readings?
correctAnswer: Logging captures night time highs and peak hour lows that spot readings usually miss
explanation: The extremes that damage pipe or cause complaints happen at night and at peak demand, times a daytime spot check rarely sees.
options: Loggers are cheaper than pressure gauges to read once
Spot readings are not allowed anywhere
Logging captures night time highs and peak hour lows that spot readings usually miss
Logging removes the need for pressure reducing valves
optionA: Loggers are cheaper than pressure gauges to read once
optionB: Spot readings are not allowed anywhere
optionC: Logging captures night time highs and peak hour lows that spot readings usually miss
optionD: Logging removes the need for pressure reducing valves
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Zone Management.

question: A new subdivision is proposed on high ground at the edge of an existing zone. What must the zone review establish?
correctAnswer: Whether the existing hydraulic grade can serve the new elevation, or a new zone or booster station is needed
explanation: Pressure at a tap depends on elevation relative to the zone hydraulic grade; high new ground may sit above what the zone can serve.
options: Whether the developer prefers a different pipe colour
Whether existing customers will move away
Whether hydrants can be removed from the old zone
Whether the existing hydraulic grade can serve the new elevation, or a new zone or booster station is needed
optionA: Whether the developer prefers a different pipe colour
optionB: Whether existing customers will move away
optionC: Whether hydrants can be removed from the old zone
optionD: Whether the existing hydraulic grade can serve the new elevation, or a new zone or booster station is needed
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Zone Management.

question: Downstream pressure in a pressure reducing valve zone climbs well above set point at night but is normal by day. What is a likely cause?
correctAnswer: The pressure reducing valve is not closing down properly at low flow, letting upstream pressure creep downstream
explanation: Pressure creep at low demand is a classic sign of a pressure reducing valve failing to throttle or seal as flow falls.
options: The pressure reducing valve is not closing down properly at low flow, letting upstream pressure creep downstream
Customers are using too much water at night
The upstream zone has been drained
The pressure gauge only works in daylight
optionA: The pressure reducing valve is not closing down properly at low flow, letting upstream pressure creep downstream
optionB: Customers are using too much water at night
optionC: The upstream zone has been drained
optionD: The pressure gauge only works in daylight
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Zone Management.

question: A flushing section has a pipe cross sectional area of 0.05 m2 and a length of 400 m. The plan flushes 3 pipe volumes. What total volume of water is used? Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: V = A x L x number of pipe volumes. Substitute the stated values: 0.05 x 400 x 3 = 60.0 m³. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place. The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.

steps: [{"l": "Relationship", "c": "V = A x L x number of pipe volumes"}, {"l": "Substitute stated values", "c": "0.05 x 400 x 3"}, {"l": "Final answer", "c": "60.0 m\u00b3"}]

question: A flush discharges 45 L/s through a main with a cross sectional area of 0.03 m2. What is the velocity in the main? Use 1,000 L per m3. Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: v = (Q / 1000) / A. Substitute the stated values: (45 / 1000) / 0.03 = 1.5 m/s. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place. The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing Design Velocity.

question: A pump delivers 50 L/s against a head of 40 m at an efficiency of 0.80 and runs for 8 hours. Use 9.81 kPa per metre of head, with power in kW from Q in L/s as P = Q x H x 9.81 / 1000 / efficiency. What electrical energy is used? Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: E = Q x H x 9.81 / 1000 / efficiency x time. Substitute the stated values: 50 x 40 x 9.81 / 1000 / 0.80 x 8 = 196.2 kWh. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place. The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.

question: Water leaves storage with a chlorine residual of 1.8 mg/L. At a given decay rate of 0.15 mg/L per hour, what residual remains after 6 hours? Round to 1 decimal place.
correctAnswer: 0.9 mg/L
explanation: Residual = initial residual - rate x time. Substitute the stated values: 1.8 - 0.15 x 6 = 0.9 mg/L. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place. The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.

question: Two pressure zones differ in hydraulic grade by 35 m of head. What is the pressure difference between the zones? Use 9.81 kPa per metre of head. Round to 2 decimal places.
explanation: Pressure difference = head difference x 9.81. Substitute the stated values: 35 x 9.81 = 343.35 kPa. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places. The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.

question: A section of main has a cross sectional area of 0.06 m2 and a length of 600 m. The plan flushes 2 pipe volumes at a flow of 60 L/s. How long does the flush take? Use 1,000 L per m3 and 60 seconds per minute. Round to 1 decimal place.

question: An upper zone hydraulic grade is 285 m and a lower zone service elevation is 195 m. What pressure is available from the head difference at that service? Use 9.81 kPa per metre of head. Round to 1 decimal place.
